90aab99008c9: What is the critical path in project management?
1da740396f56: The critical path is the longest chain of linked tasks from a project's start to its finish. Every task on it has zero slack, so a delay to any one of them moves the finish date by the same amount. Tasks off the critical path have room to slip without changing the finish.
3ea03c745e98: What is slack, or float, in a Gantt chart?
db934d5cb1fa: Slack, also called float or total float, is how many working days a task can slip before it moves the finish date: the latest it can start minus the earliest it can start. A slack of 0 puts a task on the critical path, and a negative slack means the project already runs past its planned finish.

9e106367842b: Tips for a critical path you can trust
0acd6aca3dab: <t1>Keep links accurate.</t1> The critical path is only as good as the links. A task that really waits on another but is not linked looks like it has slack it does not have. When plans change, change the link too.
64f581f50892: <t1>Put milestones on the last task’s day.</t1> A milestone a few days after the work it waits on adds slack to the whole chain, and the real critical path stops lighting up. Link the milestone and let it sit on that task’s end.
70a061e854c6: <t1>Check it weekly.</t1> The path moves as work finishes early or late. A quick look at the Slack column each week shows a task drifting toward 0 before it becomes the reason for a late launch.
fbabb57b89d4: <t1>Use a baseline to see slip.</t1> Map two planned date fields and press <t2>Set baseline</t2> to save today’s dates as the plan. <t3>Show plan</t3> draws a plan bar under every task with <t4>+2 days</t4> on the ones that slipped, and a project that runs past its planned finish shows how far: <t5>Behind by 2 workdays</t5>.
